rationale: Acceptance lens: all 5 ACs met by the current diff. Blind and edge-case lenses both ran cleanly. The edge-case lens found one real regression (CR-001): the new dedup filter can silently drop a default model from the dropdown entirely when its value is falsy/empty, where the pre-fix code at least still rendered it once as a plain row. Two blind-lens findings were triaged out: a speculative router-merge concern is moot (useProjectLLMModels already merges llmRouters into the list before LLMSelector sees it, per technical-analysis.md), and a dedup-by-value-not-identity concern is low-risk since value is treated as the unique selector key everywhere else in this file. One blind-lens test-quality note (a redundant assertion in 'marks that single row as the default') is minor and not blocking. 2 dismissed, 1 deferred-as-non-blocking (minor), 1 patch finding.

business_review.criterion: AC1 — default model displayed only once
business_review.justification: options useMemo filters models by defaultLlmModel.value whenever the synthetic default row renders (!allowEmpty, the path VirtualAssistantForm actually uses); LLMSelector.defaultDedup.test.tsx asserts exactly 1 row.

business_review.criterion: AC2 — default entry clearly marked as default
business_review.justification: Synthetic row label is '${defaultOptionLabelPrefix}: ${label}' ('Default: X'); covered by premiumLayout.test.tsx's new describe block.

business_review.criterion: AC3 — Premium label on default entry when premium
business_review.justification: defaultLlmModel.isPremium/isRouter now copied onto the synthetic row (LLMSelector.tsx:188-189); premiumLayout.test.tsx asserts the meta line text is exactly 'Premium'.

business_review.criterion: AC4 — other models keep labels, shown once each
business_review.justification: Only the default model's value is filtered out of models.map; defaultDedup.test.tsx confirms the non-default model renders once with no meta line.

business_review.criterion: AC5 — search does not return duplicates
business_review.justification: One DOM row per model means PrimeReact's built-in label filter can only match once; defaultDedup.test.tsx's search test confirms exactly 1 match.

standards_review.notes: No HTML sinks, redirects, secrets, or cross-window messaging touched by this diff.

findings.problem: The new filter `model.value !== defaultLlmModel?.value` (line 194) is applied whenever `!allowEmpty`, but the synthetic default row only renders when `!allowEmpty && defaultLlmModel?.value` is truthy (line 183). When `defaultLlmModel.value` is a falsy-but-valid string (e.g. empty string), the synthetic row is skipped by the truthiness check, yet the filter still strictly matches and removes that same model from the regular list.
findings.impact: A model with a falsy `value` that resolves as the default (via explicit `isDefault: true` or the `models[0]` fallback when no model is flagged default) disappears from the dropdown entirely and becomes unselectable — a regression versus the pre-fix behavior, which at least rendered it once as a plain row.
findings.recommendation: Compute one shared boolean for whether the synthetic row is being shown (e.g. `const showDefaultRow = !allowEmpty && defaultLlmModel?.value`) and use it to gate both the synthetic-row ternary and the filter guard, so the two conditions can never diverge. Add a regression test with a model fixture like `{ label: 'Legacy', value: '', isDefault: true }` asserting it still renders exactly once.
